doap:Project.doap:name: Wimsy
doap:Project.doap:shortdesc: Cross-platform XMPP client built with Flutter.
doap:Project.doap:description: Wimsy is a cross-platform XMPP client focused on modern server support and TLS-first connections.

xmpp:SupportedXep.xmpp:note: Renders an incoming message's security label as a coloured chip, for both one-to-one chats and MUC rooms, preferring a marking derived by parsing the primary label against a known security policy and falling back to the server-provided display marking (flagged with a warning) when that isn't possible. On connect, fetches and caches the SPIF security policies loaded on the user's own server via the Spiffing Openfire plugin's policy IQHandler (urn:xmpp:sec-label:policy:0), registering them so subsequent labels can be parsed. For outgoing messages, also fetches the label catalog (urn:xmpp:sec-label:catalog:2) once per session on connect and offers a compose-bar picker (for both one-to-one chats and MUC rooms) to attach a catalog entry, or to build a brand-new label against a known policy using an interactive classification/category editor; the chosen label is attached to the next outgoing message only (not sticky across messages) and previewed as a chip while staged. The catalog is currently fetched without a "to" attribute, so it is not scoped/filtered by the intended recipient's clearance; peer-clearance-aware catalog filtering is not yet implemented, which is why status remains partial.

Certificates that fail standard CA validation (e.g. self-signed) are not accepted automatically: the user is shown the certificate's subject, issuer and SHA-256 fingerprint and asked to trust it before the connection proceeds, with the decision remembered per-server for future connections.

OpenPGP for XMPP (OX): per-account OpenPGP key pair generated via the vendored dart_pg library, with the public key published to the urn:xmpp:openpgp:0:public-keys:<fingerprint> and urn:xmpp:openpgp:0:metadata PEP nodes; the private key is stored only in secure storage, never in the Hive database.

OpenPGP for XMPP: Instant Messaging. Outgoing 1:1 messages are wrapped in an <openpgp xmlns='urn:xmpp:openpgp:0'/> element whose base64 content is an OpenPGP message encrypted to the recipient's (and the sender's own) public key and signed with the sender's private key, carrying an XML envelope/payload/body document; selectable per-conversation alongside OMEMO/OMEMO2.

OMEMO. Supports both the legacy eu.siacs.conversations.axolotl namespace (pinned to XEP-0384 v0.3.0, as deployed by Conversations/Gajim/Dino) and the modern urn:xmpp:omemo:2 namespace ("OMEMO2"), selectable per 1:1 conversation. Both share X3DH/Double Ratchet session establishment via the vendored omemo_dart library; device lists/bundles are published and fetched via PEP under each namespace's own node names. Trust is tracked per-device (TOFU by default, promotable to verified via manual fingerprint comparison) and surfaced as a padlock indicator in the chat header. The legacy-namespace payload cipher correctly uses AES-128-GCM as specified by XEP-0384 v0.3.0 (which has no ciphersuite negotiation), distinct from OMEMO2's AES-256-CBC+HMAC-SHA-256, via a small additive hook in the vendored omemo_dart library that lets the payload cipher be substituted while reusing its X3DH/Double Ratchet session machinery. For the legacy namespace, our own identity key is a genuine Curve25519 (X25519) keypair signed via XEdDSA (see https://signal.org/docs/specifications/xeddsa), matching real libsignal-based clients (Conversations/Gajim/Dino), rather than a genuine Ed25519 identity key as used by OMEMO2 -- implemented in lib/encryption/xeddsa.dart plus small additive patches to the vendored omemo_dart library (see its VENDORING.md).

Bind 2 inline resource binding via SASL2. Sends bind element with tag in authenticate, parses bound JID from success, skips legacy IQ bind when Bind 2 completes. Also recognizes resource binding when the server conveys the bound resource solely via a full-JID authorization-identifier (XEP-0388) with an empty <bound/> element.
Includes SCRAM authentication, user-agent binding, stream resumption inline, and IAP config-version pipelining.

Renders incoming "live retractions" (observing the <retract/> request itself) with struck-through body text and a "Retracted at" timestamp chip, for both 1:1 chats and MUC rooms. Authorises each retraction against the original sender: bare JID for 1:1, and XEP-0421 occupant-id (falling back to nickname) for MUC. Also renders MAM-replayed retraction tombstones - a top-level <retracted stamp='.../> that has already replaced a message's body in the archive, since no live <retract/> was seen - with a generic placeholder body ("This message was retracted.") shown struck through and the "Retracted at" chip using the tombstone's stamp; no original body or sender authorisation is available/needed in that case, since the archive is trusted. Does not yet send retractions.

Renders incoming MUC message moderation notices (the room's XEP-0422 <apply-to/> wrapping a <moderated/>/<retract/> element, sent by the room's own bare JID) the same way as a XEP-0424 retraction - struck-through body text - but with a "Moderated at" chip instead of "Retracted at"; when the moderator supplied a reason, the body is replaced entirely with that reason instead of being struck through. The notice is matched to the original message by its XEP-0359 archive stanza-id. No sender/occupant authorisation check is performed beyond that, since the notice itself only ever arrives from the room, which has already verified the moderator's authority. Also renders MAM-replayed moderation tombstones (a <moderated by='...'> wrapping <retracted stamp='.../> and an optional <reason/>, replacing the message in the archive since no live notice was seen): when a reason is present it is shown plainly in place of the lost body, otherwise a placeholder ("This message was removed by a moderator.") is shown struck through, with the "Moderated at" chip using the tombstone's stamp. Does not yet send moderation requests.

Unlike StartTLS/Direct TLS, an untrusted certificate is not surfaced via an interactive dialog; instead the user can pin the server's expected SHA-256 certificate fingerprint (the same value/format used for WebTransport certificate pinning) and the connection is accepted only if the presented certificate matches, either via standard CA validation or that pinned fingerprint.

Sending and hosting WebXDC widgets (thread-linked file-sharing/OOB attachment plus urn:xmpp:webxdc:0 state updates with document/summary/JSON payload), using the vendored flutter_webxdc plugin to render the sandboxed mini-app, for both 1:1 chats and MUC rooms; selfAddr uses the room's XEP-0421 occupant-id when disclosed via presence, falling back to the xmpp:<bare jid> form otherwise, and selfName derived per-chat as specified. The hosted mini-app's "share to chat" requests are relayed as an outgoing text message or file attachment to the same chat. Reopening a widget replays its full, ordered update history observed during the current app session (falling back to only the latest merged state after a restart).

FAST tokens with HT-SHA-256-NONE and HT-SHA-512-NONE, token rotation, and replay-counted QUIC 0-RTT when explicitly advertised; TLS tickets persist encrypted across restarts, with durable single-use consumption and stable client identity.

Reliable multi-stream support on the web platform, including client- and server-initiated bidirectional streams with the same bare-JID routing policy as XMPP over QUIC. Discovery uses the host-meta link relation urn:xmpp:webtransport:0. Datagrams are not supported.
